title: staged-ablation-controlled-shadow-sampling-with-fallback-heuristics
author: Maya Chen
body:
Motivation: Production rollouts for new model variants can hide brittle regressions that only surface under slight changes to inputs or feature availability. Current shadow and canary flows validate end-to-end latency and basic correctness but do not exercise robustness to feature dropouts (e.g., partial context, missing metadata) or capture subtle A/B regressions caused by model reliance on auxiliary signals. This PR implements a staged "ablation-controlled" shadow sampling mechanism plus a safety-oriented fallback heuristic to automate protective degradations and rapid rollback.

Implementation summary: Adds a new RolloutController module that can (1) perform controlled ablation sampling on shadowed requests (drop or mask subsets of input features according to configurable policies), (2) route a configurable fraction of live traffic to shadow variants with optional ablations, (3) compute lightweight robustness delta metrics (response drift, token-level disagreement, confidence delta, policy hits), and (4) trigger fallback actions (route-back to stable model, rate-limit new variant, or switch to legacy pipeline) when safety gates breach thresholds. The controller integrates with existing rollout orchestration and the CanaryScheduler to support staged increases (0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20%) with automated metric evaluation windows.

What changed (high level):
- New module: orchestration/ablation_controller.go (core logic + policy API)
- Extensions to CanaryScheduler to accept ablation profiles and per-stage checks
- New evaluation metrics exported: rollout.robustness.* (drift, agreement_rate, feature_loss_sensitivity)
- Admin APIs in console for configuring ablation profiles and emergency fallback actions
- New e2e integration test that runs deterministic ablation scenarios and verifies fallback semantics
- Added docs and runbook for on-call responders describing metrics and remediation steps

Design notes: Ablation profiles are declarative and support: random token masking, metadata omission, prefix truncation, and synthetic latency injection. The sampling engine guarantees deterministic replay ids for sampled requests to allow offline debug and replay. Safety gates are defined as a conjunctive set of metric thresholds evaluated over sliding windows; gates can be per-customer or global.

Migration: Existing rollouts without ablation profiles continue to function unchanged. The new controller is opt-in; enabling ablation for a rollout requires adding an "ablation_profile" stanza to the rollout spec. Console features are feature-flagged behind "rollout.ablation.enabled".

Testing: Unit tests for ablation engine and policy evaluation. Integration tests simulate three failure modes: feature dropout, partial context, and cold-starts; verify that fallback heuristics trigger and that system falls back gracefully (no request loss, low latency degradation). Load tests run the staged ramp to ensure metric collection scales.

Rollout plan for this change: Deploy controller as a sidecar to orchestration replicas in staging, enable ablation on a synthetic traffic experiment for 48h, then enable on 0.1% production traffic for 24h. If metric gates remain green, advance to 1% and run for 48h, then to 5% and 20% with extended windows. On-call runbook and automated slack alerting are included.

Monitoring and alarms: New alert thresholds: rollout.robustness.agreement_rate < 95% (warning), <90% (critical) over 5m; rollout.robustness.confidence_delta > 0.35 (critical). Console adds a per-rollout heatmap and time-series overlays for model quality and robustness. All alerts support links to trace/replay artifacts.

Rollback and fallback semantics: There are two classes of mitigations: soft fallback (reduce novel variant weight to next safe stage, enable rate limits, continue shadowing) and hard fallback (immediate re-route to stable model and pause rollout). The fallback decision is deterministic based on gate violations plus optional human override. When hard fallback runs, the controller attaches a rollback annotation to the rollout (Linear key and operator identity) for audit.

Security and privacy: Ablation sampling happens entirely in the serving plane; sampled payloads are logged only if sampling debug is enabled and are redacted by default. New ACLs added to restrict who can craft ablation profiles. No customer PII is stored by default in replay artifacts.

Checklist (implemented):
- [x] ablation engine and sampling library
- [x] controller integration with CanaryScheduler
- [x] metrics export and dashboards
- [x] admin console controls and RBAC gating
- [x] e2e deterministic tests and load validation
- [x] runbook and Slack alerting hooks

Related tickets: Linear ENG-4521, ENG-5130; Support escalation SUP-1782 referenced for a customer incident that motivated ablation testing.
